title: A Bank Trained Its Own Foundation Model to Catch Fraud — Freddy Lecue, Wells Fargo
talk_summary: Wells Fargo pretrained a ~1B-parameter decoder-only transformer from scratch on billions of raw customer transaction records (tokenized tabular features) as a reusable backbone, then fine-tuned it for fraud detection, beating their production XGBoost on detection rate and false positives at <250ms latency. The transferable content is mostly ML-training craft (tokenization, Chinchilla scaling, mixed precision, flash attention), not agent-orchestration practice.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of thousands of hand-crafted derived features, they distilled to ~100 raw information units and let the model learn relationships between them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we step back and look at really the raw features we need, not the one that been really pre-built

takeaways.technique: Task-specific metric tied to dollar cost
takeaways.what_they_do: They judged the model on detection rate and false-positive rate because those map directly to operational cost, not on generic accuracy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the main metrics and those metrics relate right away to to dollar to cost

takeaways.technique: Latency budget as a hard design constraint
takeaways.what_they_do: They engineered to a sub-250ms inference budget because declines must happen in that window, and measured against it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you just need to have the good engineering in place to do less than 250 milliseconds
